data.name: Matelda
data.gender_notes: Matelda is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'mateleon', meaning 'maiden' or 'lady'. In Greek mythology, the goddesses Mater and Matar were associated with fertility and motherhood. Matelda embodies the strength, grace, and nurturing qualities of these divine figures. The name Matelda carries the meaning “Maiden, Lady” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Matelda usually hope their child will grow to embody maiden, lady and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of maternal love, grace, and strength.
data.etymology: Matelda belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Maiden, Lady.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Matelda total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_hebrew.name: מַתְאלֶדָה
in_hebrew.meaning: Powerful in battle, mighty in war
in_hebrew.long_meaning: From the Hebrew root words מָתָל (matal) meaning 'power, strength, battle, war' and אֵל (el) meaning 'god'. Matelda would mean 'Mighty in God' or 'God's powerful one'.

in_greek.name: Ματέλδα
in_greek.meaning: Maiden of the mountain, goddess of the sea
in_greek.long_meaning: From the Greek words ματηλή (matēlē) meaning 'maiden, young woman' and δαίδαλος (daidālos) meaning 'of the mountain' or 'goddess'. Matelda would mean 'Maiden of the mountain goddess' or 'Goddess of the sea maiden'.

in_latin.name: Matelda
in_latin.meaning: Mother of valor, mighty in battle
in_latin.long_meaning: From the Latin words māter (mother) and eldus (valor, might). Matelda would mean 'Mother of valor' or 'Mighty mother'.

in_english.name: Matelda
in_english.long_meaning: From the Old English word maegen (maiden) and the Old English word leoht (bright, shining, battle). Matelda would mean 'Maiden, shining in battle' or 'Bright maiden'.

data.cultural_impact: The name Matelda brings to mind images of strong, regal women. In popular culture, Matelda has been the name of characters who are wise, compassionate, and strong-willed. For example, Matilda Wormwood in Roald Dahl's novel Matilda is a clever and independent girl who uses her intelligence and determination to improve her life.
data.spiritual_significance: Matelda's name carries a deep spiritual meaning rooted in the ancient Greek belief in the divine feminine. It honors the maternal and nurturing aspects of the divine, representing the care, love, and protection given by a maternal figure. It also acknowledges the inner goddess within each woman, reminding us of our inherent strength and power. Matelda is a reminder of the strength and grace that comes from embracing our feminine essence.
